title: Design System: Trayce
scope: The public landing page in site/. The self-hosted product UI in web/ is a separate surface not covered here.

display.purpose: The hero headline only, cut into its plate.

headline-ledger.purpose: Section headings in the book, two 32px rules tall.

numeral.purpose: The one big row in the baseline-vs-PR seam.

body-ledger.purpose: Every line of text in the book, one per 32px rule.

label-engraved.purpose: Plate labels, the Route legend, the describer head.

label-control.purpose: Nav links, NX buttons, copy buttons, ledger row tags.

mono.purpose: Code, berths, spans, the train register.

shadows.name: plate
shadows.purpose: Any plate screwed to the panel.

shadows.name: engraving-display
shadows.purpose: The hero headline cut into its plate.

shadows.name: push-cap
shadows.purpose: Bezel and cast shadow of the NX push button.

shadows.name: pasted-print
shadows.purpose: A screenshot taped into the ledger (with rotate(-0.4deg)).

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: --ease; lit track fade and push-cap press.

motion.name: route-step
motion.purpose: The one clock: delay between successive track circuits lighting (n x 110ms), on arrival and on route setting.

motion.name: route-light
motion.purpose: Each circuit switches on as a step, not a fade, while a route is being set.

motion.name: track-fade
motion.purpose: Opacity transition on lit track outside a route-setting sequence.

motion.name: push-press
motion.purpose: Push-button cap pressing in on hover.

motion.name: copy-hold
motion.purpose: How long a copy button shows Copied before resetting.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Route lights at once; smooth scroll off.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Phone layout; the diagram switches to its narrow layout when its own width is below 640px.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Single-column hero and splits; margin rule and entry dates hidden.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Signal Box"**

The page is a railway signal box. Its two materials alternate down the page and never mix: the **panel**, an NX interlocking panel in slate enamel where every run is a route lit across a track diagram, and the **occurrence book**, a ruled grey-green ledger where the box writes down what happened. Panel sections (the hero, "What your agent actually did", the gate, replay, the quickstart) hold instruments: plates, push buttons, lamps, block instruments, a lever frame, a working timetable. Book sections (the failure, datasets, the rulebook, self-hosting) hold entries: dated headings, ledger rows, diffs, tickets, a pasted screenshot.

Color is a signalling code, not decoration. A lamp's color says a state, and an unlit element says the route isn't set. Scale does the emphasis: a 25% in condensed 800 weight, the ink-red "−50 pts" under it. The world is one fixed scheme with no dark-mode variant by design; the panel is already dark and the book already light, and the page relies on that alternation.

Motion is a single clock. Route lamps light one track circuit after another on arrival and whenever a route is set, then hold. Nothing else moves except a pressed push-button cap.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials, strictly alternating: slate-enamel panel and ruled ledger paper.
Lamps carry state: white route, red danger or fail, green clear or pass, yellow caution or underpowered.
Lit means live: unlit track and dark berths for routes not set.
Book text registered to a 32px rule pitch with a red margin rule in the content column.
Plates screwed to the panel, lettering cut into them.
One clock drives all motion: route lamps lighting in sequence.
Real data everywhere: every berth, dial, lever, and register line carries a real span, score, or command.

rules.name: The Lamps Carry State Rule
rules.body: Red, green, and yellow on the panel each mean one thing: danger or fail, clear or pass, caution or underpowered. White means a set route. A lamp color never decorates.

rules.name: The Lit Means Live Rule
rules.body: Track lights only for the route that is set; berths off that route go dark (Unlit Track text on Berth Black). An unset NX button shows an unlit lamp well, a pressed one a lit Route Lamp.

rules.name: The Two Materials Rule
rules.body: A section is either panel or book, and they alternate. Panel colors don't appear on paper and paper colors don't appear on the panel, with two exceptions: the telegram, a paper card laid on the panel, and Book Ink as the text color on a lit lamp fill.

rules.name: The Cut-In Rule
rules.body: Lettering on the panel reads as engraved into the enamel: a dark shadow above, a faint light one below (`0 -1px 0` dark, `0 1px 0` light). The hero headline carries the same cut at 2px.

rules.name: The Writing On The Lines Rule
rules.body: In the book, every line of text is 32px tall and sits on its own rule. Inline code chips drop to line-height 1 and vertical padding 0 so they never push a line off the pitch.

rules.name: The Registered Ledger Rule
rules.body: Anything placed in the book lands on the 32px pitch. A new element in a book section measures its height and margins in 32px steps or it breaks the page.

rules.name: The Screwed Plate Rule
rules.body: A plate has two screw heads in its top corners (7px radial-gradient dots, 9px in). A panel surface without screws isn't a plate.

dos: Do give every red, green, and yellow on the panel a state: danger or fail, clear or pass, caution or underpowered.
Do keep unset routes unlit: base track in Unlit Track, off-route berths dark.
Do alternate panel and book sections, and register every line and gap in the book to the 32px rule pitch.
Do keep book content right of the margin rule (120px indent) on wide screens.
Do letter the panel in condensed uppercase with the cut-in shadow, and screw plates down with two screw heads.
Do drive motion from the one clock: route lamps lighting in sequence on arrival and on route setting.
Do draw scorer verdicts as block instruments and scorer config as levers in lever colors.
Do put real values in every berth, dial, lever, and register line.
donts: Don't use a lamp color as decoration.
Don't light track or berths for a route that isn't set.
Don't add a second animation, or animate anything besides route lamps and the push-button press.
Don't add a dark-mode or light-mode variant; the world is one fixed scheme.
Don't emphasize with a new color where scale will do.
